historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds two-component mapping, signed artifacts, dependency order, rollback and OOB ownership.

original_test_intent: Upgrade or downgrade the specified HMC and FPGA through the OOB path, activate them safely in the approved order, and demonstrate correct active versions with recovered management, baseboard and host operation.
original_method: Map HMC controller/bank and FPGA device to exact OOB resources; record current/target versions and directions; verify separate signed images or vendor bundle composition, compatibility, dependency/order and rollback; preserve baseline; execute approved task(s), operator performs activation/power cycle; independently read HMC and FPGA active versions and verify BMC/host/power/GPU health.
manual_activity: Firmware owner resolves HMC/FPGA targets, images/directions/order and rollback; operator authorizes update/activation and owns OOB recovery; agent performs only approved tasks.
required_inputs: Exact HMC controller/bank and FPGA device/inventory IDs
Separate signed images or authoritative bundle manifest and hashes
Per-component current/target versions and upgrade/downgrade directions
Redfish targets/tasks, activation/power, rollback, console/OOB and maintenance approval
safety_requirements: Never infer both devices from one HGX_0 label
Do not update until image-to-component and order/atomicity are proven
Follow returned task resources and preserve existing BMC/SEL logs
Require recovery path before any controller or logic write
Stop after any component/task/activation anomaly; no second update or retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate per-component identities, artifacts and dependency plan
Capture baseline and execute only approved OOB task sequence
Collect active versions and management/baseboard/host recovery
engineer_actions: Authorize state changes and power activation

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A generic OOB flash suggestion does not prove separate HMC and FPGA coverage; literal Redfish credentials, TLS bypass and Task 1 are unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Submit the vendor-approved signed per-component image(s) or atomic bundle to mapped authenticated OOB targets, monitor returned tasks, activate in approved order and read HMC/FPGA versions independently.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Both HMC and FPGA, upgrade/downgrade and AC activation remain; no component map, direction or order is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a dependency-aware two-component transaction ledger recording staged/active versions, task boundaries, power event and independent post-recovery health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Prevents one aggregate HGX task/version from concealing a skipped or failed component.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: GPU firmware recovery does not substitute for HMC control-plane or FPGA logic recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Updating HMC can disrupt the controller needed to observe FPGA progress; vendor ordering and independent recovery access are mandatory.

project_override_considerations: Board firmware owner defines whether HMC and FPGA ship as an atomic bundle, supported mixed-version states and downgrade/rollback paths.
expected_evidence: HMC controller/bank and FPGA device/target map
Signed artifact hashes, bundle manifest and per-component before/target/after versions
Sanitized requests plus each returned task state/message
Management, baseboard, GPU/PCIe and SEL/dmesg/BMC health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Two named firmware classes and upgrade/downgrade recovery are represented by one generic DGX bundle/HGX_0 target, without per-component direction, order or inventory mapping.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Static review is complete; execution awaits component-specific project data and approvals.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row270 Wistron-NV GPU-00263-V002: identify HMC controller/bank and FPGA device targets behind HGX_0; decide separate images versus atomic bundle, per-component upgrade/downgrade direction and current-target versions, dependency/order, task/activation semantics, rollback and OOB recovery.

review_improvement: Makes both components independently traceable and prevents aggregate task/version evidence from masking missing HMC or FPGA coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: HMC firmware governs management functions while FPGA logic may govern board behavior; their update dependencies and recovery interfaces can differ. If HMC restarts mid-sequence, the observer for an FPGA task may disappear, and a mixed-version state may be unsupported. Component-specific before/after evidence and vendor-defined ordering are therefore necessary even when packaged as one bundle.
